Definition: to rub or strike the hands together (in exultation)
BiblicalUsage: The word means to clap the hands together, and it is used for joy and for spite alike. The mountains and hills shall break forth into singing and the trees of the field shall clap their hands when God's people go out with joy, and the floods clap their hands with them. But Ammon clapped his hands and stamped his feet and rejoiced with all his despite against the land of Israel, and God heard that clapping too.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe clapping is the body's praise, and the trees themselves will do it when God's people come home. I hold that the same hands can clap in joy or in spite, and God tells the two apart.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
